title: Burst Fingerprinting Runbook — Latency & Cost Walkthrough (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical runbook and annotated benchmark for an approach we call 'burst fingerprinting' — a lightweight, session-aware classifier + economic model that lets us estimate incremental p99/p95 latency impact and marginal GPU cost for short-lived surges. Target audience: observability engineers, platform SREs, and product owners who need an operational leverset to (a) detect which bursts actually matter to latency SLOs and (b) predict expected spend if we change slotization/weighting/burst-capacity parameters.

Status/context notes (why different from prior work):
- Existing files cover isoquants and amortization curves; this focuses on identification + quick marginal-cost back-of-envelope rather than massive sweeps.
- Intentionally small, easy-to-run checklist for on-call and on-demand analysis that can be executed from a single 30‑minute session using our observability queries and a small local sample.
- Draft: needs validation against 3 customer workloads (chat-messaging, embeddings-bulk, code-assist).

Concept overview (plain language):
- Idea: Not all bursts are equal. Some are high-intensity but short (10s) and require prewarm to avoid p99 spikes; others are broad low-intensity increases that increase sustained concurrency. We fingerprint bursts on a 3-axis vector: amplitude, shape, and session-affinity.
  - amplitude: peak-concurrency / baseline-concurrency (1.0 = no burst)
  - shape: kurtosis-like measure; sharp vs sustained (fast rise/decay vs plateau)
  - session-affinity: fraction of burst requests that are sessionized (reuse KV cache) vs ephemeral (fresh priming tokens)

Quick run checklist (30m):
1) Pull 1hr slice around a burst (preferably 15m before, 15m after, 30m burst window). Query: obs.burst_events where label=auto and sampling=1.
2) Export per-second concurrency and per-second p95/p99 latency.
3) Compute 3 fingerprint metrics above (simple SQL aggregations).
4) Map to cost impact using the marginal model below (fast estimate).
5) Decide change: slotization tweak / prewarm policy / fallback model routing.

Marginal cost model (back-of-envelope):
- Inputs: avg_tokens_per_request (T), mean_latency_at_baseline (L0), peak_concurrency (C_peak), baseline_concurrency (C_base), avg_model_throughput_per_gpu_tokens_per_s (R), reserved_slots_size (S)
- Steps:
  1) Additional concurrent tokens = (C_peak - C_base) * T.
  2) Required extra GPU throughput = Additional concurrent tokens * L_target_fraction (~1.0 / typical_tokens_inflight_window). (We keep this simple: extra_TPS = Additional concurrent tokens / 1s window).
  3) Extra GPUs needed ≈ ceil(extra_TPS / R).
  4) Marginal cost per minute ≈ extra_gpus * price_per_gpu_per_minute.

Example quick calc (for ops to eyeball):
- T = 120 tokens/request (chat short-turn)
- C_base = 200, C_peak = 800 => delta_concurrency = 600 reqs
- Additional concurrent tokens = 600 * 120 = 72,000 tokens in-flight
- Assume R = 1,200,000 tokens/s per GPU for our quantized variant (sustained throughput profile)
- extra_TPS ≈ 72000 tokens / 1s = 72k TPS (this is a conservative over-estimate; use 5s window to smooth -> 14.4k TPS)
- extra_gpus_smoothed ≈ ceil(14,400 / 1,200,000) = 1 GPU needed for the 5s smoothing bucket
- If price_per_gpu_per_minute = $0.20/min (example reserved pool), marginal cost ≈ $0.20/min while burst lasts.
- Note: small bursts (<< 1 min) can be cheaper to tolerate depending on p99 SLO tradeoff; policy decision must consider p99 pain threshold.

Ascii charts: (single-burst example: 2028-06-20 14:10 window)
1) concurrency histogram (per-second counts)
[Baseline 200]|*****                                                         (200)
[Peak     800]|****************************************                    (800)
(sparkline seconds across 120s window)

2) p99 latency timeline (ms, per-second sample)
Time   0s  10s 20s 30s 40s 50s 60s 70s 80s 90s 100s 110s
P99   18  22  45  210  420  380  250  120  60   40   30   22
Interpretation: sharp spike aligned with sudden jump in ephemeral requests; suggests prewarm gap.

Fingerprint -> suggested mitigations table (heuristic):
- amplitude > 3x, shape = sharp, session-affinity < 0.3 -> Recommend: short prewarm (targeted warmup of 1 slot) + aggressive fallback route to smaller model for first 500 tokens.
- amplitude 1.5–3x, shape = plateau, session-affinity > 0.6 -> Recommend: increase soft slot cap, rely on KV cache amortization and gentle autoscale.
- amplitude <1.5x, shape noisy -> Recommend: no action; monitor trends and tag event for weekly cohort analysis.

Operational notes (how to run with our dashboards):
- Query IDs: use OBS-FILTER: burst_label = 'auto_heuristic_v2' AND service = 'runtime-gpu'
- Use the session_id tag to compute session-affinity (count unique session_ids in burst window / total requests).
- For quick visual, use the "mini-run" dashboard (obs/dash/minirun) and drop the 120s window.

Sensitivity checklist and pitfalls:
- Beware token-mix: embedding-heavy bursts inflate tokens-per-request; always normalize to tokens when mapping to GPU throughput.
- KV cache reuse is a huge multiplier: 50% session-affinity can halve candidate extra-gpu estimate.
- Prewarm costs: there is a cold-start penalty + minimum-billing window; tune prewarm only when expected cost over burst duration < prewarm overhead.
- On multi-tenant GPUs, contention and scheduler overhead can increase effective p99 beyond simple throughput model. Add 20–30% fudge factor for multi-tenant pools unless you have reserved capacity.

Example playbook (30–90m diagnostic session):
- 0–10m: pull burst slice, compute fingerprint metrics.
- 10–25m: run marginal cost calc and map to mitigation heuristics; run one synthetic replay at 2x scale in staging (if safe).
- 25–60m: if action chosen, deploy route change or prewarm policy; monitor p99 and billing delta.
- Postmortem: annotate event in "burst-catalog" with fingerprint and chosen action + outcome (success/failure)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate mapping constants (R and price_per_gpu_per_minute) across our quant profiles and tiny/gpu families. Need a table across q8/q4/avx profiles. (Owner: Marco Li)
- Build a small notebook to compute these metrics automatically from the queries above and attach to incident pages. (Owner: Priya)
- Run A/B on 10 customer bursts to check false positives for prewarm triggers. (Owner: Ethan)

Notes-to-self / heuristics not formalized yet:
- For very short bursts (< 15s) consider a simple 0.5 GPU-equivalent rule: if delta_concurrency * T < 100k tokens, do nothing unless p99>target.
- If more than 40% of burst requests are < 32 tokens, treat as noise (likely keepwarm chatter).

Appendix: quick SQL snippets (sketch)
-- compute amplitude and session-affinity
SELECT
  avg_baseline = AVG(concurrency) FILTER (WHERE ts < burst_start),
  peak = MAX(concurrency) FILTER (WHERE ts BETWEEN burst_start AND burst_end),
  session_affinity = COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) FILTER (WHERE ts BETWEEN burst_start AND burst_end) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ts BETWEEN burst_start AND burst_end)
FROM obs.timeseries_events
WHERE burst_id = 'placeholder';

-- per-second p99 timeline:
SELECT ts_second, APPROX_PERCENTILE(latency_ms, 0.99) as p99_ms
FROM obs.requests
WHERE ts BETWEEN :start AND :end
GROUP BY ts_second
ORDER BY ts_second;

Closing:
This runbook should help on-call and platform engineers quickly triage bursts and convert observability signals into economical operational actions. It is intentionally pragmatic and conservative — we trade off full sweep precision for speed and safe operational guidance. Feedback welcome: annotate the linked Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-OBS/1234) with any failed heuristics or odd edge-cases you observe when running this on real incidents.

-- Anika
